Orsted AS Names New Chief Operating Officer as Company Pursues Growth in Renewables

COPENHAGEN, June 12 — Denmark’s Orsted AS announced on Wednesday the appointment of Lars Mikkelsen as Chief Operating Officer, as the electric utilities firm looks to strengthen its leadership team amid ongoing expansion in offshore wind and renewable energy projects.

Mikkelsen, 54, will assume the role effective August 1, replacing Ingrid Rasmussen, who is stepping down after six years in the position. The company said Rasmussen will remain with Orsted AS in an advisory capacity until the end of the year to support the transition.

“We are delighted to welcome Lars to the executive team,” Orsted CEO Mads Nørgaard said in a statement. “His extensive experience in large-scale infrastructure and proven leadership in project delivery will be instrumental as we continue to grow our global footprint and deliver on our ambition to become the world’s leading green energy company.”

Mikkelsen previously served as Chief Projects Officer at Nordwegian Power Systems, where he oversaw the development and commissioning of renewable facilities in Scandinavia and the UK. He holds a master’s degree in engineering and brings more than two decades of experience in the energy sector.

Orsted AS, headquartered in Copenhagen, is a leading developer of offshore wind farms, with operations spanning Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific. The company has set a target to install 50 GW of renewable capacity by 2030, up from 15 GW at the end of last year.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, citing Mikkelsen’s track record in project management and operational efficiency. “Orsted’s ability to execute complex projects on time and within budget is crucial for its long-term competitiveness,” said Sophie Jensen, senior analyst at the Danish Energy Federation. “Bringing in someone with Lars Mikkelsen’s background reinforces their commitment to operational excellence.”

The Danish Wind Industry Association also reacted positively. “Leadership continuity and fresh expertise are both needed as the sector navigates supply chain challenges and evolving regulatory frameworks,” said director Henrik Lauridsen.

Shares in Orsted AS were up 0.7% by midday on the Copenhagen exchange. The company said it will announce further details on its updated operational strategy at its next capital markets day in September.
